---
title: "Fit distributions"
---


```{r}
# Load required package 
require("fitdistrplus")
library(fitdistrplus)
```


## Example with normal

```{r}
# Example data set 
x = c(42,37,50,28,33,46,39,55,31,49,31,33,36,44,40.5,27,52,44.8,38,43,30,47,35,51)
hist(x) #ugly hist
```


```{r}
# Fit distribution to data using maximum likelihood 
fit1 <- fitdist(x,distr= "norm", method = "mle")
```

```{r}
# Generats plots comparising empirical cdf with fitted cdf, and histogram with fitted pdf
plot(fit1)
```

```{r}
# Extract goodness of fit as an AIC-value 
AIC(fit1)
```


```{r}
# Extract the parameters for the fitted distribution. You use these values to sample or calculate things from the distribution 
fit1$estimate
```

```{r}
# For example, if the distribution is normal one can calculate the 95th percentile like this
qnorm(0.95,mean=fit1$estimate[1],sd=fit1$estimate[2])
```



## Example with data bounded in 0 and 1

```{r}
# Example data set
x = c(0.45, 0.08, 0.02, 0.001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.86, 0.006, 0.01, 0.26, 0.63, 0.20, 0.007, 0.73, 0.51, 0.002, 0.03, 0.38, 0.02, 0.04)
hist(x) #ugly hist
```


```{r}
# Fit distribution to data using maximum likelihood 
fit2 <- fitdist(x,distr= "beta", method = "mle")
```

```{r}
# Generats plots comparising empirical cdf with fitted cdf, and histogram with fitted pdf
plot(fit2)
```

```{r}
# Extract goodness of fit as an AIC-value 
AIC(fit2)
```


```{r}
# Extract the parameters for the fitted distribution. You use these values to sample or calculate things from the distribution 
fit2$estimate
```

```{r}
# For example, if the distribution is beta one can generate 200 random numbers like this
rbeta(200,shape1=fit2$estimate[1],shape2=fit2$estimate[2])
```

Let us compare two candidate distributions 

```{r}
# Fit distribution to data using maximum likelihood 
fit3 <- fitdist(x,distr= "gamma", method = "mle")
```

```{r}
# Generats plots comparising empirical cdf with fitted cdf, and histogram with fitted pdf
plot(fit3)
```

```{r}
# Extract goodness of fit as an AIC-value and compare the two candidate models. Lower AIC is better model
AIC(fit2) # beta
AIC(fit3) # gamma
```


```{r}
# Extract the parameters for the fitted distribution. You use these values to sample or calculate things from the distribution 
fit3$estimate
```

```{r}
# For example, if the distribution is beta one can generate 200 random numbers like this
rgamma(200,shape=fit3$estimate[1],rate=fit2$estimate[2])
```
